project_type: Python prosodic analysis library being extended into a Streamlit app for contrafactum generation
test_framework: None currently - will add basic pytest tests
test_command: python -c "from pyesia.spanish_poetry_functions import syllables, rhyme, rhyme_scheme, perform_analysis; print('OK')"
verification_instructions: 1. Install requirements: pip install -r requirements.txt && pip install -e . 2. Run: streamlit run app.py --server.headless true (verify it starts without errors) 3. Test imports: python -c 'from generator import generate_contrafactum; from validator import validate_lyrics; from repair import repair_lyrics; from prompts import SYSTEM_PROMPT; print("All imports OK")'
environment_constraints: OPEN_INTERNET - can install any packages. Python 3.11.14 via pyenv. No API keys available for OpenAI/Anthropic so LLM calls cannot be tested end-to-end, but code structure and non-LLM logic can be validated.
contribution_requirements: No CONTRIBUTING.md exists. Keep changes minimal and focused on MVP.
key_patterns: pyesia/spanish_poetry_functions.py contains all prosodic analysis functions. Key functions: syllables(word), tonic_syllable(syllables_word), detect_synalephas(...), rhyme(word1, word2), rhyme_scheme(poem), clean_punctuation(text), perform_analysis(poem_path). The perform_analysis function reads from a file path - we will need to adapt to work with text strings directly. The rhyme_scheme function takes a list of verse strings (not a file). The module uses 'from spanish_poetry_functions import *' style imports internally.
directory_structure: pyesia/ - main package with spanish_poetry_functions.py (all analysis logic) and pyesia.py (class wrapper). Root level - setup.py, README.md, LICENSE.txt. New files (app.py, generator.py, validator.py, repair.py, prompts.py, requirements.txt) will be created at root level.
